What is really helpful is that there are activites at 3 different levels for all areas, which makes planning a breeze.  I wish I had found this book years ago instead of wasting my time making file folder games,etc.  Along with the three centers represented in this book I will have a writing and listening center--and I am set for the year!

Differentiated Literacy Centers is an outstanding and thorough resource that is based upon sound research.  The structure of this book made it easy to read and to quickly find key elements: tips on organization and time management of centers, comprehension, fluency and word study activities, in addition to corresponding blackline masters.  Options for planning are outlined in different frameworks.  All questions that you may have are answered and the author includes a quick-glance summary for each area.  I highly recommend this book!

As I was looking through the various options for modest-sized, relatively current world map to put on my office wall, I came across NewSpaceView's US-centered World Map. I've never seen a map that had the US prominently featured in the center of the page - well, more towards the upper central part, but you get the idea. The typical world map we've all seen: the North, Central, and Southern Hemispheres are to the left, Europe and Africa are in the middle, and Asia and Oceania (Australia, Micronesia, New Zealand, and other nearby islands) are to the right, with some of these lands often wrapping back around on the left side.

Then I realized that for anyone living in North, Central, or South America, it's actually a great idea to use a map where these regions are in the center, because of course we want to know how far other countries from us when we are travel planning! It makes it so much easier for those in the Americas to figure out how many time zones away something really is and other important considerations. Why other regions don't do something similar is to be centered around their part of the world is beyond me. Maybe they do, but I've rarely seen maps that are adjusted that way. There's nothing wrong with wanting your part of the world to be in the front and center of a map. If anything, it makes one appreciate the amount of distance between countries or lack thereof very clearly.

The map itself is really nice, with excellent color contrast between different continents and countries, as well as subtle border lines between nations and the different states in the USA. I also like that the map doesn't just feature the capital of each country or in the different states of the USA, but does note many larger cities as well. Some of the smaller countries are harder to see because of the map's scale, but for a map that is 52.5 inches left to right by 31.5 inches top to bottom, it's actually impressive as to how much detail is included for each country. The lamination quality is excellent, it's on both sides of the sheet and the map's finish is smooth and glossy throughout. The countries seem up-to-date for now (early 2017), with South Sudan noted on this version.

I'm very pleased with this map's overall quality compared to previous world maps I've owned. In fact, I would buy other maps from this company if they produce more with this high quality or with the same attention to detail. If you live North, Central, or South America, this map will be very relevant and appreciated by you.
summary: Map centered on the Americas (North, Central, and South)

If you are looking for a map of the world with a true representation of land mass and location then the Peters Projection Map is the place to go. It shows countries to scale and without the western bias so evident in maps of the past where wealth is equated to size and made Europe as big as South America. This is invaluable when teaching geography as you can see more clearly how the various continents and islands fitted together and how they have shifted apart. It also gives a fair representation of land size and location and makes you appreciate just how vast, and overlooked, places like Africa are. It may seem like a small deal to use a new type of map, but in a world looking to resolves many issues and find a certain peace it always helps to have as a starting place a fair, accurate and equal representation of your place in it.

The life of a stay-at-home mother, filled with laundry, dishes, finicky taste buds and too little adult interaction, can be an overwhelming one. It can also be a joyous time of laughter, pretend, sticky kisses and stolen moments. The trick is in choosing the joy over the mundane.

Cindy Sigler Dagnan pretty much summed it up when she said, "All of us want to be there for our children--we just don't want to lose ourselves in the process." With sections covering the supermom syndrome, time management, financial management, personal growth, spiritual growth, and marriage, she provides realistic goals and solutions to make the most of our years at home. She even finishes out her book with recipes that are kid-friendly, yet adult palatable.

It has been a long time since I've picked up a book on "the life of a mom" that has been so helpful and encouraging. There were chapters that made me want to pat myself on the back--Look! Something I have achieved!--and chapters that made me want to be a better person.

My biggest complaint is that I would be in the middle of a chapter and would feel inspired to put the book down to go forth and do. She gave me the inspiration to "Relax in the rhythm that causes [me] to dance, not trudge, through life."

As usual, each month has an appropriate country or village scene depicting activities from the 19th century. People are shopping, riding in sleighs down snowy streets and up hill sides, the homes and stores are inviting, and a lovely Christmas tree sits in the village square. It is the idealized rural village that continues to have a grasp on the imagination of so many of us, especially when you from time to time find yourself longing for a slower pace of life, even on just a temporary basis. The calendar can bring that to you! I have purchased Ms Nelson's calendars for years, and am never disappointed. I've ordered this for my wife each year for several years.
The 2015 edition is of the same quality as previous years; that it was printed in China hasn't affected its visual appeal. It's printed on good quality heavy stock, with the hanging hole reinforced with a metal ring. Altogether it's of a much higher quality than most "themed" calendars and much more interesting to look at.

It has a different pair of 12 inch x 13 inch pages for each month so you'll need 13" x 24" of wall space to hang it.

The calendar page is clear and very easy to read; it includes international holidays etc., which are useful. There's enough space each day to make your own notes, if you're inclined.

The quality of the artwork and the number and variety of seasonal subjects that Marjolein chooses for each month's painting make them pleasing enough to stand on their own apart from the calendar.

If you're a gardener, interested in "nature" subjects, or just like something good to look at instead of just a list of dates, this is something you'd enjoy.  In the past, I thought it lacked information about what was in each painting, but I've come to think that it's not necessary.  After all, there's nothing wrong with having to do your own research.

If I don't write a review for the 2016 and subsequent editions when they are published, it will be because they are as good as I've come to expect.

With this map, you can seriously get the best of both worlds, as it combines elements of both Political and Physical. Although some parts of the map can get quite cramped and the physical aspects can be a bit difficult to see (especially the northern Balkans), but some things that really stand out with this map are:

1.) Most European maps cut off from some areas I consider extremely important, especially to European history, such as Northern Africa, Part of the middle east (Israel. Iraq, and Syria are included).

2.) The shear amount of information put into this map that makes it an absolute gem. I doubt any European map does so much with the space provided.

3.) The absolute coolest part of this map is the curvature visible in the map. Most maps use a Cartesian plane, making them very flat, which can seriously distort Northern parts of Europe, but this one curves the map, preserving the shape of the continent as well as providing an extremely accurate scale. reviewText: This is my 4th year in a row to get one..the best Austin Calender PERIOD
Best calendar! A whole year of fun, new, things to do locally!

Cool find; I search Free Fun in Austin and Meetup weekly for fun events for my child and I, so this will be much easier than going through all of the entries on there.  And I also forget about events - so it will be nice to have it in one place.

They have it cheaper locally - see http://austin.bigweekendcalendars.com for retailers (ex. HEB sells it for $12.99).

Comes with a little bucket list.  Has moon cycle.  They do not take or solicit money in exchange for including events, which is cool.  Made by Austinites.

It has ~10 activities (ex. duck tour, cycling, cruises) at the top of each month and ~15 events per month.  Suggestions for food (Salt Lick), tacos

Example of events: Austin City Limits, Bat Fest, AustOberfest, Nerd Night, Chuy's Children Giving to Children Parade, Eeyore's Birthday Party, Free Day of Yoga, Fun Fun Fun Fest, Hero Con, No Pants Day, Pecan Street Festival, Polar Bear Splash, Trail of Lights, Zilker Pops Concerts...

Now only if I could combine my yearly photo calendar with this one...too much work...
summary: Nice to have events organized and all in one place; cheaper bought locally

reviewText: I've been buying this calendar for several years now, and I just love it! Such a great resource for finding fun things to do around town. There are also lists of activities to do in a given month, such as ice skating in December. Highly recommended for Austinites!

What a treasure trove of cool, fun, traditional, educational, spectacular, whimsical and weird things going on in Austin! This calendar is great if you want to plan for out of town guests or are a business and want to avoid hosting an event on a "big" Austin weekend.
I like the layout this year. There's plenty of room to write in my own events without sacrificing information. I have really enjoyed reading all the entries. But I'll admit I've only gotten through March. I'm saving some of the fun for our next rainy day.
In my opinion anyone who's not a recluse should own one of these calendars. And heck...if you never leave your house you get to attend hundreds of cool events vicariously - it's a win win!
summary: Best Resource for Great Austin Happenings!
